newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable amid ample liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable amid ample liquidity.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in thin late trading on Monday despite ample money market liquidity, dealers said.
"Volume is thin. The focus is on liquidity," one U.S. bank dealer said. He said liquidity was ample but the dollar failed to gain sharply on fears of a possible tightening.
Spot rupiah was at 2,390.5/91.1 at 0900 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,390.0/91.00. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,390.9/91.1 and 2,391.0/91.5 respectively.
The ample market and absence of overnight bilateral papers (SBIs) from the central bank sent overnight money to a low of three percent before settling at five percent.
"Operators do not know how the liquidity condition will be on Friday. The weekly tax payments will be due and it's also the month-end. Liquidity might be tight," another dealer said.
"The market is still driven by liquidity. People seem to have no worries on Tuesday tax payments," the dealer said.
Dealers said swap rates declined slightly but the downside seemed limited because of a possible tight market.
Overnight swap was at -0.05/par and tom/next at 0.05/0.08.
"Swaps are pretty cheap at present following the ample market. But a broad fear of a possible tightening on Friday is there, which gives support to swap rates," opne said.
One-month swap edged down to 9.0/10.0 from 9.75/10.50, two to 23.25/23.75 from 23.75/24.25, three 36.0/36.5 from 36.75/37.25 and six to 74.5/75.5 from 75.0/77.0 points.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention band at 2,380/2,572 and the conversion band at 2,380/2,428 on Monday.
The bank depreciated the rupiah by two points last week, after lowering it by three points the previous week.
